claims.text: The target eutectic HEA initially contains FCC and ordered B2 phases, with B2 precipitates or lamellae in an FCC matrix.
Intermediate-temperature aging increases local chemical ordering within the B2 phase.
Increasing B2 local chemical order produces a continuous, highly ordered B2 network.
A continuous ordered B2 network acts as a brittle percolating path.
The continuous ordered network restricts dislocation mobility in the FCC phase by pinning dislocations at FCC/B2 interfaces.
Dislocation pinning at FCC/B2 interfaces promotes crack initiation along brittle B2 boundaries.
The cited prior evidence directly supports the proposed dislocation behavior in ordered domains.
In Al0.5NbTa0.8Ti1.5V0.2Zr, a continuous ordered B2 matrix was associated with 2032 MPa yield strength and only 4.7% compressive fracture strain.
In Al0.5NbTa0.8Ti1.5V0.2Zr, solutionizing produced a weakly ordered BCC structure containing nanoscale B2 regions, with more than 60% compressive ductility and a yield strength of 1065 MPa.
Annealing Al0.5NbTa0.8Ti1.5V0.2Zr at 600 °C produced an inverted morphology consisting of a continuous disordered BCC matrix and discrete approximately 50 nm B2 precipitates.
At higher aging temperatures, B2 local chemical order destabilizes through disordering or phase separation.
At higher aging temperatures, the B2 morphology coarsens or loses continuity, thereby breaking the brittle percolating network.
Breaking the continuous B2 network restores ductility by enabling dislocation transmission through the FCC matrix and reducing phase-boundary stress concentrations.
Intermediate aging at approximately 500–600 °C will produce a fracture strain below 5%.
Aging above approximately 700 °C will restore ductility to above 15%.
Yield strength will peak in the intermediate aging regime because of local-order strengthening and then decrease at higher temperatures because of coarsening or disordering.
The embrittlement regime is bounded by temperatures at which B2 local order and B2 connectivity are maximal; below it ordering is insufficient, while above it ordering or connectivity declines.
Classical impurity-driven grain-boundary embrittlement and grain coarsening are excluded as the primary causes.
The proposed temperature-series experiment will measure B2 ordering, B2 connectivity, fracture strain, yield strength, and dislocation structures.

The hypothesis is falsified if the ductility minimum fails to coincide with high B2 ordering or continuity, if recovery fails to coincide with disordering or loss of continuity, or if grain-boundary segregation is identified as the primary cause.
